explanation: erdosproblems.com/626: with h^{(m)}(n) the maximal chromatic number of an n-vertex graph of girth > m, does lim log h^{(m)}(n)/log n exist (and what is its value)? The Lean h m n is sSup of chromatic numbers of graphs on Fin n with egirth > m (bounded by n, so a true maximum); the statement ∀ m, ∃ L with log h/log n → L encodes existence, with the value addressed in the h_odd/h_even variants. For m ≤ 2, h = n and the limit is 1, consistent. Faithful.
